A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LongSpec. All 23 pages of v2 and 18 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures. Reformatting and section removals do not prevent reliable matching.

before.justification: V2 reports original decoding-speed and acceptance-length measurements on long-context benchmarks and AIME24, together with ablations, throughput experiments, and prefill-length analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original LongSpec experiments and reports additional retrieval-baseline comparisons, math-benchmark results, and a Flash Noisy Training ablation.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same sliding-window draft architecture, target KV-cache reuse, shared embeddings and LM head, Anchor-Offset Indices, Flash Noisy Training, and Hybrid Tree Attention. V3's pseudocode documents existing procedures; it does not establish an algorithm or model change.

E1.justification: Math-reasoning evaluation expands substantially from AIME24 alone to AIME24, AMC, MATH500, and Minerva Math in v3 Table 3. The five summarization/code-completion benchmarks and the training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V3 adds Prompt Lookup Decoding (PLD) across all five target-model configurations and five datasets in Table 1. Token Recycling joins the appendix comparisons for Vicuna-7B and LongChat-7B. The appendix EAGLE comparison for LLaMA-3.1-8B is removed; MagicDec and the other EAGLE comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V3 newly reports a with/without Flash Noisy Training control, although its detailed experimental setup is unspecified. Retained experiments keep the same training budgets, long-context temperature settings, 32k reasoning-output cap, beam widths, and inference hardware and precision.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 newly reports that Flash Noisy Training increases acceptance length by 14.7%, with improvements concentrated on the final speculative tokens. The Anchor-Offset ablation, attention-latency breakdown, throughput analysis, and prefill-length analysis are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix H states that all reported results have zero error bars across runs because evaluation and inputs are deterministic. V3 removes this reporting statement without supplying replacement uncertainty estimates, run counts, or seed information.

E6.justification: V3 adds PLD and Token Recycling scores and math results of 45.16 tokens/s on AMC, 44.51 on Minerva, and 48.36 on MATH500. Existing Table 1 values and AIME24's 42.63 tokens/s and 2.25× speedup are unchanged. The reported 2.34× reasoning average summarizes expanded coverage, not an AIME24 gain. LLaMA-3.1-8B EAGLE results are removed.

T1.justification: V3 removes Section 3.4 and v2 Appendix D, including Theorem 3.1, formal network definitions, assumptions, the MLE error bound, its proof, and supporting lemmas. This deletes the approximation, distribution-shift, and generalization analysis. Appendix C's attention-aggregation proposition and proof remain mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: The three central innovations and the maximum 3.26× long-context speedup claim remain unchanged. The abstract and introduction broaden the reasoning claim from 2.25× on AIME24 to a reported 2.34× across four math datasets; the conclusion retains its original scope.

C2.justification: V3 removes v2 Appendix H's explicit decoder-only Transformer restriction, RNN incompatibility discussion, and proposed broader testing. It adds an explanation that PLD can slow generation when retrieval is minimal. Interpretations of attention optimization and prefill-length stability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix G adds pseudocode specifying offset sampling, query/KV slicing, padding, and output projection for existing techniques. Training and inference details move from Appendix E to D without substantive changes. V2's explicit LongSpec code-availability statement and repository link are removed; this does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V3 adds references and positioning for PLD, Token Recycling, vLLM, and the expanded math benchmarks, while removing the two Zhang references supporting the deleted theory. The main related-work discussion and positioning around lightweight drafting versus full-target-model drafting remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative order remain intact. Local edits update author information and benchmark discussions, remove theory and discussion sections, add a pseudocode appendix, and shorten one case study. V3 also incorrectly refers to its reasoning results as Figure 3 rather than Table 3.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reformats the document, including converting single-column appendices to two columns and restructuring equation and case-study layouts. The AIME24 bar chart becomes an expanded four-dataset table, and comparison tables gain baseline rows. Most retained figures reuse the same artwork.

improvement.justification: The added retrieval baselines, math benchmarks, ablation, and pseudocode strengthen empirical support and implementation clarity. These gains coexist with removal of the draft-error analysis, applicability and uncertainty disclosures, code-access pointer, and some EAGLE evidence. The core results and attention-correctness proof remain intact. The tradeoff between stronger evaluation and reduced theoretical and reporting completeness does not establish a reliably clear net quality direction.
